insights.statement: Procurement's €3.0M a year applies 12% to the full €25M, including €1.1M of rush freight the price cut does not touch: the real gross saving of the full move is €2.87M a year, and €7.80M over 2026-2028 after the €0.8M switching cost
insights.decision_relevance: The saving the board is asked to approve is overstated before risk is even counted

insights.statement: Supplier B runs a single plant and stopped twice in three years (9 and 14 days); with all volume on it, a repeat would cost €4.0M of gross margin, more than the €2.93M the full move earns over a 70/30 split in 2026-2028, because the incumbent can only cover up to 60% of volume at two weeks' notice
insights.decision_relevance: The incremental 1.08 EUR M a year of the full move is bought with an uncovered continuity risk
insights.caveat: Two events is a small sample: a single 14-day stoppage (2.4 EUR M) would not by itself reverse the comparison; stoppage losses under the 70/30 split are not quantified in the sources

insights.statement: A 70/30 split (Supplier B 9% on 70% of volume, incumbent 4% on the 30% it keeps) saves €1.79M a year and €4.88M over 2026-2028 after €0.5M switching, against €3.80M for the full move once a repeat of Supplier B's stoppages is counted
insights.decision_relevance: Gives the board an approvable alternative that keeps 62% of the gross saving and a second plant
insights.caveat: Requires the incumbent's 4% offer and Supplier B's 9% tier to be confirmed in writing

insights.statement: Rush freight is our forecasting problem, not a supplier problem: €0.65M of the €1.1M (59%) sits in months the invoices flag as 'our forecast errors', and neither supplier offer reduces it
insights.decision_relevance: The 1.1 EUR M is the only further lever toward procurement's 3.0 EUR M target and sits with demand planning
insights.caveat: Upper bound; the achievable reduction is not sized in the sources
